findings.claim: Implemented hub-installed luxnix-vault-site-lifecycle contain|rotate|resume FQDN. Containment checks the exact PKI role domain, persists a root-only role-keyed marker, denies the site policy, destroys its Secret ID accessors, and revokes only issued tokens matching both site policy and AppRole metadata. Enrollment and reconciliation share its lock and cannot clear containment; uppercase enrollment names are refused to prevent case aliases.

rotate FQDN --output-directory NEW_DIR requires completed containment, preserves non-secret KV fields, replaces shared_secret using the observed KV v2 CAS version, verifies the resulting value/version, and exports six protected installer-compatible enrollment files. Partial failure requires fresh containment before retry. resume FQDN --accept-consumer-verification requires rotated state and removes only the local marker; explicit luxnix-vault-reconcile-hub-sites FQDN then restores policy.

Certificate issuance now authenticates afresh from AppRole files after the certificate cache check and before issuance, unsetting the expired bootstrap token. Auth errors expose no response details; offline authentication failure may retain only a still-valid matching cached certificate. AppRole token TTLs remain 1h/4h; newly reconciled roles explicitly issue accessor-revocable service tokens.

Verified API semantics for AppRole accessor destruction, token accessor revocation including descendants, and KV v2 compare-and-set. Lifecycle helper sends payloads over stdin and redacts API failures.

Migration requires deploying these wrappers on the authoritative hub, preserving /var/lib/luxnix-vault-site-lifecycle across rebuild/recovery, deploying the fresh-auth client module, and using a reviewed short-lived custodian policy. The policy needs site-bound PKI role/CA reads, site ACL write, role Secret ID list/create/destroy and role-id read, KV node read/write, plus privileged token accessor list/lookup/revoke. Do not put the affected site policy on the operator token. Deliver the new bundle over authenticated encrypted transport, update both NetworkNode consumers and verify old rejection, then resume/reconcile and restart the dependent client chain.

Integration review identified that ordinary timer restart retains a still-valid revoked cached certificate. Added root-only luxnix-vault-reissue-hub-client-certificate on hub-PKI clients: runtime force marker bypasses cache checks and all offline success fallbacks, is cleared only after publishing certificate/key/CA, and is retained after authentication/issuance failure. No certificate is revoked automatically.

Read-only integration review confirms lifecycle CLI matches documented contain/rotate/resume arguments, action+site-scoped JSON success occurs only after successful action, and resume removes only the marker without restoring policy. Found false disk-free delivery claim: installed Ansible copy action serializes content to tempfile.mkstemp under C.DEFAULT_LOCAL_TMP. Root was notified to correct implementation/claims and distinguish alternative manual installation instructions.

gaps: No live Vault, host, credential, deployment, consumer database or remote-state operation was performed. Actual new-machine enrollment, old-ID/token rejection, both node-record adoption, offline recovery and elapsed breach recovery time require controlled operator acceptance.
Full host derivation evaluation/build and repository configuration checks remain root integration work; only module syntax and host discovery were run by this worker.

Containment markers coordinate these hub-local wrappers; other administrative Vault sessions and alternate hubs must be serialized and must not overwrite the deny policy. Preserve the marker directory in disaster recovery. Vault audit destination and custodian ownership remain operator requirements.

Accessor enumeration cannot enumerate pre-existing batch tokens. Review deployed AppRole token types and await their bounded expiry or use explicit custodian containment before restoring policy. Service tokens with unexpected policy provenance cause a fail-closed blocker; accessor lookup races with expiry may require rerunning containment.

Certificate revocation and receiver enforcement are a separate worker boundary. Keep network/application containment until certificate and application rejection are demonstrated. No retiring KV versions are destroyed; retained history requires custodian retention policy.

Role names retain the existing punctuation-normalizing mapping for compatibility. Exact-domain checks and role-keyed containment prevent accidental scoped revocation/containment bypass, but operators must not enroll colliding FQDN aliases as distinct sites.

Forced-reissue marker is under /run and survives service failure, not reboot. Rerun the explicit helper after a reboot until replacement acceptance completes; preserve network/application containment. Node provisioning is RemainAfterExit=true and needs an explicit restart on both consumers.
